done_when: forge doctor and doctor --fix treat AGENTS.md as changed by hand only when the text between the forge:begin and forge:end lines was edited outside Forge; edits outside those lines never hold it, and doctor --fix refreshes the block while keeping them byte for byte; a command test covers a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release, with a hand edit outside the block (refreshed) and one inside it (held)

findings.body: An outside-only edit is still held when Git checks AGENTS.md out with CRLF, for example with core.autocrlf=true. HEAD and index blobs contain LF, but the working block is read without newline conversion, so working == head fails even though the client edited only the suffix. Both doctor commands then report uncommitted changes and --fix skips the block. Git documents this checkout/index distinction in its [configuration contract](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-coreautocrlf). Client attributes shipped by src/forge/sync.py:278 add only merge rules, so they do not prevent this configuration. The new test's CRLF case changes only the prefix and suffix while constructing an LF block (tests/test_doctor_preserves_rules_outside_forge_block.py:27–29); it therefore passes despite this failure. Compare the working block and Git blobs in the same Git-normalized representation while retaining raw outside bytes for writing, and cover an outside-only edit after a real CRLF checkout.
findings.title: Not done: forge doctor and doctor --fix treat AGENTS.md as changed by hand only when the text between the forge:begin and forge:end lines

findings.body: This loop validates every historical AGENTS.md blob using _agents_block, which calls sync._span. That validator refuses unmatched or duplicated markers (src/forge/sync.py:143–144). Consequently, a repository that once committed a broken marker and subsequently repaired it cannot run doctor or doctor --fix successfully, even after a later Forge upgrade supplied a valid block. The command stops with a broken-block refusal referring to the current file, which is already valid; editing it cannot remove the offending historical blob. Validate the current file normally, but handle malformed historical versions conservatively without aborting the entire doctor command.
findings.title: Do not reject a repaired file because an historical block was malformed

why: forge doctor holds a client's whole AGENTS.md as 'changed by hand' when the last commit touching it added the repo's own Review rules outside the forge:begin and forge:end lines (where Forge asks for them), so doctor won't refresh Forge's own block (reported by a client session)
